For "PREMIER PLAY" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

Tomorrow's count on "PREMIER PLAY" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2414.headline: How the prize money is divided

2415.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Double The Money", about half are still unsold. The game is about halfway through its run, with two of three top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

If you play "Double The Money" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2415.headline: Tickets sold so far

2416.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "Loaded with $2,000s" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The numbers for "Loaded with $2,000s" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
2416.headline: Early stage or late

2419.body:
"Bronze 7s" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $2,777 was claimed in the latest numbers. Unsold tickets still hold one of the original four. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

The numbers for "Bronze 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2419.headline: A top prize was just claimed

2420.body:
A $177,777 top prize on "Silver 7s" was claimed earlier this week. The game started with three top prizes and has two top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Everything above about "Silver 7s" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2420.headline: Someone claimed a $177,777 prize

2421.body:
"Gold 7s" has gone over a month without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a quarter of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $577,777 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "Gold 7s", with every prize level included.
2421.headline: Good news: no big claims

2422.body:
"Platinum 7s" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of its unclaimed prize money, about two-thirds is in wins under $2,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The table below shows the full count for "Platinum 7s", with every prize level included.
2422.headline: The prize mix in this game

2426.body:
"HAUNTED HUNDREDS" has 124,388 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $50 prize, with 999 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The numbers for "HAUNTED HUNDREDS" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
